description: Backend: update ResourcesService.submit() to auto-approve resources uploaded by admins or lecturers (status=APPROVED, isOfficial=true). Update ResourcesController to pass the full User object to submit() instead of just user.id so the service can read the role without an extra DB lookup. No module changes needed — UsersModule is already imported in resources.module.ts.
steps: Open backend/src/modules/resources/resources.controller.ts. Change the POST / handler body from `return this.service.submit(user.id, body)` to `return this.service.submit(user, body)` — pass the full User object.

Open backend/src/modules/resources/resources.service.ts. Change the submit() signature from `submit(uploaderId: string, data: Partial<Resource>)` to `submit(uploader: User, data: Partial<Resource>)`. Import User from '../users/entities/user.entity'. Inside the method, derive `const isPrivileged = uploader.role === UserRole.ADMIN || uploader.role === UserRole.LECTURER;` then set `uploaderId: uploader.id`, `status: isPrivileged ? ResourceStatus.APPROVED : ResourceStatus.PENDING`, `isOfficial: isPrivileged` when creating the entity.
Verify: run `cd backend && npm run lint` — zero errors. Then run `npm run build` — TypeScript compiles with no type errors.
acceptance_criteria: `npm run lint` passes with zero errors in the resources module
`npm run build` compiles successfully (no TypeScript errors)
submit() method signature accepts a User object and sets status=APPROVED and isOfficial=true when role is ADMIN or LECTURER
submit() still sets status=PENDING and isOfficial=false for STUDENT role
findings: submit() signature changed from (uploaderId: string, data) to (uploader: User, data). Controller passes full User object. Service derives isPrivileged from uploader.role and sets status=APPROVED + isOfficial=true for ADMIN/LECTURER, status=PENDING + isOfficial=false for STUDENT. User and UserRole were already imported in resources.service.ts. No new imports needed. IMPORTANT: npm run lint/build could not be verified locally — node_modules/.bin is empty because npm install failed with EPERM file-lock errors (backend process running and holding locks on typeorm/openai dirs). All 50 tsc errors observed are pre-existing environment issues (wrong typeorm version cached) across 34 files, none of which are the two files modified by this feature. The code changes are logically and type-structurally sound.
